idea: ClimaAgro provides a B2B2C hyper-local climate alert system for agribusiness buyers sourcing from smallholder farmers in Peru.

selected_gap.title: Personalized, hyper-local climate alerts via WhatsApp
selected_gap.pain: Small farmers depend on generic forecasts or informal word-of-mouth, leading to poor decisions and crop losses. No existing service delivers actionable, parcel-specific advice through an accessible, low-tech channel like WhatsApp.
selected_gap.why_now: WhatsApp penetration in rural Peru exceeds 80%; El Niño intensifies climate volatility; insurers and cooperatives seek tools to reduce loss ratios and improve farmer engagement.
selected_gap.evidence_needed: Pilot with 500 farmers to measure reduction in crop loss versus control group; message open rates and action compliance data.

friedman_scores.note: No founder background provided; assumed generalist team. Needs deep agri/climate domain expertise in Peru.
B2B2C model addresses large agribusinesses; TAM of smallholder agriculture in Peru is potentially >$1B if including crop value at risk, but actual serviceable market may be smaller initially.
Extremely painful: crop losses from weather events destroy farmer income and disrupt supply chains; current workarounds are ineffective.
Some generic weather apps and government alerts exist, but hyper-local WhatsApp advice with actionable recommendations is a clear differentiator.
Founder likely has personal connection to agriculture or climate tech, but not evident from idea description alone.
WhatsApp penetration, improved satellite data availability, and increasing climate volatility make this timely.
Similar B2B2C agri-insurance and advisory models exist in India (e.g., CropIn) and Africa; validates model but not direct competitors.
Requires long-term relationships with agribusinesses and farmers; founder would need to be committed for 5+ years.
Scalable via WhatsApp and satellite data, but requires onboarding agribusinesses and farmer networks; per-customer acquisition may be heavy.
Climate tech for agriculture is a huge and underserved space; hyper-local actionable advice is a strong angle.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Do not wait for the perfect idea
yc_rule_scores.note: Idea is well-defined and ready for testing; could start pilot with minimal product.
Not clear if founder is fully committed; one idea at a time is assumed.
The B2B2C model shows understanding of agribusiness procurement workflow, but depth could be improved.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Build at the edge of AI
yc_rule_scores.note: Uses satellite data and models, but no proprietary AI; explainability and recommendations could leverage LLMs for personalization.
Positioned as 'protect supply chain', reduce volatility, improve loyalty – outcome-focused.
Targeting entire Peruvian smallholder agri supply chain is ambitious; but first step is feasible.
No mention of learning from failures; should have clear testable hypotheses.
Agriculture requires domain expertise; low trust between farmers and generic services; ClimaAgro can build trust via agribusiness partners.
Advisory process is key; but product is also the alert system; need to ensure process integration.
Risk of building before real demand; evidence needed from pilot.
Subscription to agribusinesses based on number of farmers or alerts; aligns with outcome pricing.
Satellite data costs are variable; WhatsApp is cheap; need to manage scaling costs.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Do not bolt AI onto legacy
yc_rule_scores.note: Solution is new, not legacy; uses modern data sources and distribution.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Cover domain, model, and operations fluency
yc_rule_scores.note: Team needs fluency in agronomy, climate science, and operations; not fully demonstrated.

vc_rubric_scores.rationale: No founder data given; assumed average team. Need domain expertise in Peruvian agriculture and climate data.
TAM of smallholder agriculture in Peru is large (>$1B when including crop value and supply chain disruptions), but SOM is modest initially. Growing due to climate change.
Hyper-local actionable alerts via WhatsApp are novel and defensible via data integration and partner relationships. Moat is distribution and trust.
No evidence of pilot, LOIs, or revenue. Idea is pre-traction. Need pilot results to validate.
Subscription model to agribusinesses is reasonable; LTV:CAC unknown, margins likely >60% if scalable. But unit economics unproven.
Generic weather alerts and some agri-tech startups exist, but none focus on hyper-local WhatsApp advice for Peruvia smallholders. Need to out-execute.
No financial data provided. Burn rate and runway unknown. High risk of undercapitalization pre-pilot.
Main failure mode: low farmer adoption of advice or low willingness of agribusinesses to pay. Mitigated by low-cost channel and proven demand.

vc_verdict.reason: Weighted score 5.55 below threshold; weak: traction

decision: Proceed with caution. Validate through pilot before full build-out. Focus on closing one agribusiness partner and measuring impact.
next_experiments: Conduct 20+ interviews with agribusiness buyers in Peru to validate willingness to pay and desired outcomes.
Launch a WhatsApp-based MVP for 50 farmers with manual curation of alerts to test engagement.
Run a controlled pilot with 500 farmers comparing crop loss between alert recipients and control group.
kill_criteria: After 3 months, no agribusiness partner signs a pilot agreement or LOI.
Message open rates below 50% or action compliance below 20% in pilot.
Unit economics show LTV:CAC < 2x after pilot costing.
_iteration_one_liner: We deliver hyper-local, actionable climate alerts to smallholder farmers via WhatsApp, paid for by agribusiness buyers to de-risk their supply chains.
